notes.read_side: Both families read the WORKING TREE, not HEAD: an uncommitted corpus edit is a legitimate observation. Record `git status --porcelain` beside the numbers.
notes.equal_mode: corpus.index.tracked_files and corpus.pointers.commit_total are change detectors, not invariants: adding a corpus file or a new commit citation moves them and must move the baseline with it (same convention as verifiers/baseline.json).
notes.zero_mode: zero-mode ids ignore `expect` at evaluation time; they are listed so the baseline names every id the script checks. A zero-mode violation exits 1 even under --no-baseline.
notes.out_of_scope_context: corpus.pointers.commit_quoted_excluded and corpus.pointers.report_pointers_other are context, not checks. The first counts `commit `<token>`` citations fully enclosed in double quotes (quoted meta-findings, e.g. corpus/lessons/round-6-aggregator-audit.md:45; live: 2 — the second is the same idiom quoted inside corpus/knowledge/claim-census-round12.md). A double-quoted report pointer is recorded in `report_pointers_quoted[_detail]` as context (the mechanism repaired in round 12: the tokenizer no longer swallows a leading `"`; the live tree has 0 such tokens, so the rule is exercised by `--self-test` and by `verifiers/fault_injection_corpus.sh` fault (h), which asserts the counters: context +1, checked population unchanged). Round 12's independent derivation names this boundary and its shared blind spot in corpus/knowledge/independent-verification-round12.md §3/§3b.
notes.reproduce_before: Against a clone of d49dfa5 with the landed scripts copied in (README pre-fix): report_dead=10/19, commit_total=18, commit_nonhash=1, exit 1 — the DRIFT the round-11 edit cleared; the round-12 independent derivation reproduces the same ten dead sites and the same non-hash site there. The same clone run twice is byte-identical under --json.
notes.environment: exit 2 when the target is not a git repo / corpus/README.md is unreadable; exit 3 when this file is absent and --no-baseline was not passed.
notes.commit_total_scope: `corpus.pointers.commit_total` counts HEX-SHAPED citations only (`commit `<7–40 hex>``) that also resolve; a non-hash `commit` token is carried by `corpus.pointers.commit_nonhash` and is NOT part of this count. The round-12 independent derivation publishes the same number as `commit_hex_total` alongside a wider in-scope total — the adjudication is recorded in corpus/knowledge/independent-verification-round12.md §3 item 1.
notes.hermeticity: Pointer resolution is host-anchored: absolute and `~` pointers resolve against the live filesystem, not against the clone. With the host `.ufo` hidden behind a private tmpfs, a green clone goes dead = checked (both instruments identically). `python3 verifiers/verify_corpus_integrity.py` is therefore only meaningful on a host that carries the lane-report tree.
